name: Conduct insurance tele-interviews
sector: medical laboratory and health services (insurance medical evidence)
summary: A tele-interview replaces the paper health questions of a life insurance application with a recorded phone interview. A trained tele-interviewer calls the applicant at the booked time, confirms identity and gives the recording notice, reads the insurer's health, lifestyle and family history questions with reflexive follow-ups, types the answers and releases the report and recording to the insurer. A typical interview takes about 25 minutes, but missed calls, unprepared applicants and dropped lines force rebooking, and team leads review a sample of recordings before release.

baseline.org_archetype: The tele-interview centre of a large Canadian laboratory company's insurance medical evidence line, with about 65 bilingual and multilingual interviewers working from Brampton and remotely for every Canadian life insurer.
baseline.notes: Starts when a booked interview reaches an interviewer's schedule and ends when the report and recording are released to the insurer or the order is closed. Booking the first appointment is part of order management. The self-service scheduling portal launched in January 2023, after the reference period.

trigger: A tele-interview booking from the order desk appears in the tele-interview scheduler.
end_state: The interview report and recording are delivered to the insurer and the case review queue, or the order is closed after the advisor and insurer are told the applicant cannot be reached.

volume.seasonality: Follows insurance sales; evening and Saturday slots fill first, so interviewer schedules peak outside office hours.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's process map (9,000 to 17,000 a month), itself an estimate.

Trained professionals take the health history by phone (dyn_ti). FTE: 60 of the 65 tele-interviewers, close to hands-on time (about 37 minutes per interview including missed calls and rebooking) times 13,000 interviews. Wage near the Job Bank 64409 Ontario median; Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Team lead, insurance customer care
roles.department: Insurance order desk and case management

evidence.note: Team leads review a sample of recorded interviews and handle problem files with advisors and carriers; share of the 12 team leads is an estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Tele-interview scheduler and interview questionnaire software
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
Insurance Order Management System with Paraweb ordering and iCARE status hub
Electronic results delivery to insurers (ACORD and custom formats)

steps.name: Route the booking to an interviewer's schedule
steps.description: The tele-interview scheduler places the booked slot in the calendar of an interviewer who speaks the applicant's language and is trained on the insurer's questionnaire, and sends the applicant a reminder before the appointment.
outputs: scheduled interview on an interviewer's list

evidence.note: Multilingual interviewers (dyn_paraweb); reminders before the appointment (dyn_sched, described for the 2023 scheduler; the 2019-2022 scheduler is assumed to send at least an email or call reminder).

steps.name: Prepare for the call
steps.description: Shortly before the slot the interviewer opens the order and the insurer's questionnaire in the interview software, reads the applicant's age, coverage amount and product, and checks which modules the insurer wants (health, lifestyle, vocation, travel, business or financial questions).

error.defect_description: Wrong insurer script or module opened.

evidence.note: Questionnaires vary by insurer and may include lifestyle or vocation modules (dyn_ti). The wait is the lead time from booking to the appointment (mode one day, up to five), an estimate.

steps.name: Call the applicant at the booked time
steps.description: The interviewer dials the applicant within the booked hour on the recorded contact centre line. Interviews that run long push later calls toward the end of their window.

evidence.note: Applicant contacted within 1 hour of the booking time (dyn_tibro, dyn_prep). The 18 percent missed-call share is an estimate; the 2023 scheduler was built partly to avoid no-shows (dyn_sched).

steps.name: Verify identity and give the recording and privacy notice
steps.description: The interviewer confirms the applicant's full name, date of birth and address against the order, states that the call is recorded and that the answers go to the named insurer for underwriting, and asks the applicant to confirm they agree to continue. Applicants who are driving, at work or without their medication list are offered a new time.

error.defect_description: Interview done with the wrong person or without the recording notice.

control.basis: PIPEDA consent principle and Privacy Commissioner guidance on recording customer calls: notice of recording and its purpose and consent before collecting health information

next.condition: needs an interpreter for a language not covered
not a good time or not prepared

evidence.note: Notice of recording and purpose required (opc_record); call backs when clients are not prepared (wp2015). Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Join a telephone interpreter
steps.description: For a language no interviewer on shift speaks, the interviewer dials the interpreter service, briefs the interpreter on confidentiality and the call's purpose, and conferences the applicant back in; the interview then runs through the interpreter.

error.defect_description: Answers lost or shortened in interpretation.

next.condition: interpreter not available now; rebook with interpreter

evidence.note: Multilingual interviewers are offered (dyn_paraweb); use of an outside interpreter line for other languages is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Ask the health questions with reflexive follow-ups
steps.description: The interviewer reads each of the insurer's health questions word for word from the script; every 'yes' opens reflexive questions on dates, diagnosis, treatment, medications and doses, tests, time off work and the treating physician's name and address, and the interviewer types the answers into the questionnaire software as the applicant speaks.

error.defect_description: Missing date, dose or physician detail, or a disclosure typed under the wrong question.

evidence.note: Reflex questions capture as much history as the applicant can give (dyn_ti); preparation list of doctors, medications and dates (dyn_tibro). The split of the 25-minute interview between sections is an estimate.

steps.name: Ask the lifestyle, family history and other modules
steps.description: The interviewer asks the family history (parents and siblings, ages and causes of death), height and weight and recent changes, tobacco, alcohol and drug use, driving record, travel and risky activities, and any vocation, business or financial questionnaire the insurer ordered.

error.defect_description: Lifestyle detail incomplete, for example no quantity for alcohol use.

evidence.note: Family history and lifestyle details listed in the preparation guidance (dyn_tibro); lifestyle or vocation questionnaires (dyn_ti).

steps.name: Read back the disclosures and close the call
steps.description: The interviewer summarises the conditions, medications and physicians disclosed, corrects anything the applicant changes, confirms the family doctor's contact details for a possible APS, records the applicant's verbal confirmation that the answers are true and complete, and explains that the insurer may order other requirements.

error.defect_description: Read-back skipped and an error is not corrected.

evidence.note: A health professional may contact the applicant for other services (dyn_ti); undisclosed doctors lead to a second APS (wp2015), which is why physician details are confirmed. Times are estimates.

steps.name: Complete the interview report
steps.description: After the call the interviewer finishes the report in the questionnaire software, adds notes on anything unclear, attaches the call recording, and runs the software's completeness check before marking the interview complete.

error.defect_description: Report finalised with a blank required field or a typing error.

next.condition: disclosures trigger the insurer's follow-up rules

evidence.note: Transcripts and recordings are delivered to the carrier (dyn_sched). Branch shares are estimates.

steps.name: Flag disclosures that call for more evidence
steps.description: Where the insurer's instructions say a disclosure needs more evidence (for example a heart condition or diabetes calls for an APS, or the applicant reports a new doctor), the interviewer records the flag and the physician details on the report so the underwriter or order desk can order it.

error.defect_description: Flag missed or wrong physician recorded.

evidence.note: Some insurers let the tele-interview vendor order follow-up requirements (27 percent for age and amount requirements and 10 percent for the APS in soa2011). The 22 percent share of interviews with a follow-up flag is an estimate.

steps.name: Review a sampled interview against its recording
steps.description: The team lead listens to the recording of interviews picked by the quality sample (all interviews of new interviewers, a few percent of others), compares it with the report, checks the script was read as written and the recording notice given, and scores the interview.

control.basis: Insurer service agreements and the company's quality program: sample review of recorded interviews before release

next.condition: answer unclear; applicant must be called back

evidence.note: Recording for a stated purpose such as quality assurance (opc_record). The sampling rate and error rates are the author's estimates; no published figures were found.

steps.name: Correct the report after review
steps.description: The interviewer reads the reviewer's notes, replays the relevant part of the recording and corrects the report, for example a missed medication dose or a disclosure placed under the wrong question.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of correction effort.

steps.name: Call the applicant back to clarify an answer
steps.description: When the recording leaves an answer unclear (a date, a medication, a physician), the interviewer phones the applicant, verifies identity again, asks only the open question on the recorded line and updates the report.

error.defect_description: Applicant cannot be reached and the report is released with a note.

evidence.note: Call backs for missing information are a known delay (wp2015); times are estimates.

steps.name: Release the report and recording to the insurer
steps.description: The system sends the completed report and the recording to the insurer in its format through the electronic delivery channel, marks the interview complete in iCARE for the advisor and passes the report to the case review queue.

evidence.note: Transcripts and recordings delivered to the carrier (dyn_sched); delivery batch timing is an estimate.

steps.name: Retry the call within the appointment hour
steps.description: The interviewer tries the applicant again, and any second number on the order, two or three times within the booked hour and leaves a voicemail saying when they will try again.

evidence.note: Calls happen within the booked hour (dyn_tibro); retry pattern and success share are estimates.

steps.name: Call back after a dropped call
steps.description: When the line drops, the interviewer calls the applicant back right away and resumes from the last completed question; if the applicant cannot continue, the rest of the interview is rebooked.

error.defect_description: Interview resumed at the wrong question, leaving a gap.

evidence.note: If disconnected, the tele-interviewer contacts the applicant to continue (dyn_tibro). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Rebook a missed or interrupted interview
steps.description: Following the problem file procedure, the interviewer or scheduling desk calls, texts or emails the applicant to offer a new slot and books it; after repeated no-shows or no reply the file goes to the team lead.

error.defect_description: New slot booked in the wrong time zone.

next.condition: applicant not reachable after repeated attempts

evidence.note: No-shows follow the standard problem file procedure: contact the applicant to reschedule or the carrier to advise of the delay (dyn_sched). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Tell the advisor and insurer about the delay
steps.description: The team lead sets the order to a problem status in iCARE and emails or phones the advisor and the insurer's new business contact with the attempts made, asking them to have the applicant call in or confirm whether to close the order.

evidence.note: Carrier advised of the delay under the problem file procedure (dyn_sched).

steps.name: Wait for the advisor or insurer to respond
steps.description: The advisor reaches the applicant and the applicant calls in or books a new time, or the insurer cancels the requirement because the application was withdrawn or decided without it.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of advisor response and withdrawal.

exceptions.name: Applicant misses the call
exceptions.description: The applicant does not answer within the booked hour; the interview is rebooked and repeated no-shows go to the advisor and insurer.

exceptions.name: Applicant not ready
exceptions.description: The applicant is driving, at work or without the medication list and asks for another time.

exceptions.name: Interpreter needed
exceptions.description: No interviewer on shift speaks the applicant's language, so an interpreter is conferenced in or the interview is rebooked with one.

exceptions.name: Dropped call
exceptions.description: The line drops mid-interview and the interviewer calls back to resume or rebooks.

exceptions.name: Quality review finds an error
exceptions.description: The reviewer finds a missed detail or misplaced answer; the report is corrected or the applicant called back.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from booking reaching the interviewer schedule to report released

evidence.note: Synthesis: most interviews are booked a day or two ahead and released the same day; the company says self-service booking (2023) cut turnaround by 2 business days by removing callouts, and insurers adopted tele-interviews partly to shorten turnaround (soa2011). No published distribution was found.
dyn_prep gives 25 to 30 minutes.

benchmarks.unit: minutes after the booked start within which the applicant is called

pain_points.description: Applicants miss the booked call or are not prepared, so interviews are rebooked and some files stall until the advisor intervenes.

evidence.note: The 2023 scheduler was built to remove telephone tag and avoid no-shows (dyn_sched); call backs when clients are not prepared (wp2015).

pain_points.description: Answers typed while the applicant speaks miss dates, doses or physician details, which surface in review or later as underwriter questions.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Quality review depends on listening to recordings, which takes about as long as the interview itself, so only a small sample is checked.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

pain_points.description: Each insurer has its own script and follow-up rules, so interviewers must be trained on many questionnaires.

evidence.note: Insurer-specific questionnaires (dyn_ti); vendor ordering of follow-up requirements varies by insurer (soa2011).

sources.title: Tele-interviews
sources.supports: Tele-interview is the applicant's health history taken by phone by a trained professional for the insurer; questionnaires include reflex questions and may include lifestyle or vocation questionnaires; approximately 25 minutes depending on the history; applicants should have their physician's details, medications, ID, heights and weights and travel dates ready; a health professional may contact the applicant for other services the insurer requires.

sources.title: Prepare for your medical exam (applicant resources)
sources.supports: The interviewer calls within the hour of the scheduled appointment; the interview usually runs 25 to 30 minutes and can take longer depending on answers and medical history.

sources.title: Booking your telephone interview is easier than ever before (tele-interview brochure)
sources.supports: Applicant is contacted within 1 hour of the start of the booking time because some conversations run long; if disconnected the interviewer calls back to continue; applicant should have the family doctor's contact details, current medications and doses, dates of diagnoses, height and weight, family history and lifestyle details (alcohol, tobacco, drugs, driving, risky activities).

sources.title: The model laboratory's insurance testing service scheduler user guide
sources.supports: Self-service tele-interview scheduler launched 9 January 2023 to remove callouts and telephone tag, improve turnaround and avoid no-shows; reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before; interview transcripts and recordings are delivered to the carrier; for a no-show the team follows the standard problem file procedure, contacting the applicant to reschedule or the carrier to advise of the delay.

sources.title: Paraweb: place your order and review status
sources.supports: Tele-interview service offers flexible appointment times and multilingual interviewers; orders and status available 24/7.

sources.title: Report of the Society of Actuaries Improving the New Business Process Survey Subcommittee
sources.supports: Tele-interviews were added for protective value and because they decreased total turnaround; 27 percent of respondents let the tele-interview vendor order age and amount requirements and 10 percent let it order the APS; about a quarter said tele-interviews reduced turnaround.

sources.title: Recording of customer telephone calls
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Organizations must inform customers that a call is being recorded and why; consent is implied when the customer continues after notice, express consent may be needed for sensitive information; purposes must be stated narrowly; retention of recordings must be limited.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 3: Consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Meaningful consent is required to collect, use and disclose personal information; express consent is generally required for sensitive information.

sources.title: Why does it take so long to get my policies issued?
sources.supports: Tele-interviews are rescheduled or need call backs for missing information when clients are not prepared; undisclosed doctors lead to a second APS; tele-interviewing is one of the changes that reduced turnaround.

sources.title: Wages: Customer service representative, call centre in Ontario (NOC 64409)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 21.50, high 33.17 dollars (Labour Force Survey 2023-2024).

assumptions: The 18 percent missed-call share, 5 percent not-ready share, 10 percent quality sample and 22 percent follow-up flag share are estimates; no published rates were found.

Disclosures that call for more evidence are recorded on the report for the insurer or the order desk; the organisation file's process map has no link from tele-interviews back to order management, although in practice a disclosure often leads to a new APS or paramedical order.
Applicants confirm their answers verbally on the recorded line; some insurers also send the transcript for signature with the policy, which is outside this process.
Rebooking is done by the interviewer or the tele-interview scheduling desk; the organisation file has no separate scheduler role for this team.
Phone work is given a desk work share of 0.7 to 0.9: it is done at a desk in the interview software but consists of talking with the applicant.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
